title: Regulated efficacy phrases need a matching fact and compliance sign-off
examples_bad: clinically proven to fade dark spots
source_ref: ASCI Code, Chapter I (truthful and honest representation)

title: No medical or therapeutic claims for cosmetics
source_ref: Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 (cosmetic vs drug claims)

title: Environmental claims must be specific and substantiated
No unqualified superlatives or rankings
source_ref: ASCI Code, Chapter I.4 (claims of superiority)

title: Endorsement claims need evidence in the fact ledger
source_ref: ASCI Code, Chapter I.1 (substantiation of claims)

title: No fairness or skin-lightening claims
source_ref: ASCI guidelines for skin lightening and fairness products

title: A study or percentage claim needs its study footnote
params: {"when_regex": "(?i)\\b(clinically|dermatologically tested|study|studies|trial|participants|proven to)\\b|\\b(reduc\\w*|improv\\w*|fad\\w*|boost\\w*|increas\\w*|lighten\\w*)\\b[^.!?\\n]{0,40}?\\bby\\s+\\d+\\s?%|\\b\\d+\\s?%\\s+(reduction|improvement|increase|fewer|less|more)\\b", "must_regex": "\\*[^\\n]*\\b(study|participants)\\b", "message": "Study and percentage claims need the footnote DL-02: \"*In-house study, 48 participants, 2026.\""}

title: Offers and discounts need "T&Cs apply"
params: {"when_regex": "(?i)(\\b\\d+\\s?% off\\b|\\bdiscount\\b|\\boffer\\b|\\bsale\\b|\\bBOGO\\b)", "must_regex": "(?i)\\bT&Cs? apply\\b", "message": "Promotions must say \"T&Cs apply\" and link to the terms."}

title: Paid or gifted creator posts must disclose the partnership
params: {"when_regex": "(?i)\\b(gifted|sponsored|in partnership with|collab|PR package)\\b", "must_regex": "(?i)(#ad\\b|#sponsored\\b|\\bpaid partnership\\b)", "message": "Add #ad or \"Paid partnership\" at the start of the caption."}
source_ref: ASCI guidelines for influencer advertising in digital media (2021)

title: Never mention unreleased product codenames
source_ref: Aurelle Brand Book v1.3 §9 Confidential information

title: Text in images meets WCAG contrast (4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text)
Every non-decorative image has alt text written by a person
Capitalise each word in multi-word hashtags so screen readers can read them
source_ref: Aurelle Brand Book v1.3 §6.4 Social accessibility

title: Tone is warm and energetic, never hype or pressure
params: {"instruction": "Flag sentences that rely on hype, urgency pressure, fear of missing out or exaggerated promises. Energetic and warm is fine; shouting and pressure are not."}
examples_good: Meet the new Vitamin C Brightening Serum.|Your skin, a little brighter every morning.
examples_bad: HURRY!!! Last chance EVER to fix your skin!|Don't be the only one without it.

title: At most one exclamation mark; no shouting in capitals
Avoid all-caps words (brand name and standard acronyms excepted)
Speak to the reader as "you"; never talk down
params: {"instruction": "Flag sentences that lecture, shame or talk down to the reader about their skin."}
examples_bad: Stop ruining your skin with cheap products.

title: Use active voice unless the action matters more than who does it
params: {"instruction": "Flag passive constructions where the actor is known and matters (VT08)."}
examples_good: We tested the serum on 48 people.
examples_bad: The serum was loved by everyone.

title: Lead with the main point
params: {"instruction": "Flag posts whose first sentence does not state the product or the main message (GM02)."}
examples_good: Meet the Vitamin C Brightening Serum: brighter-looking skin in 8 weeks.*
examples_bad: We have been thinking a lot about mornings lately, and about what they mean to all of us.

title: Every post has one clear call to action
params: {"when_regex": "^[^.!?\\n]+", "must_regex": "(?i)\\b(shop|discover|try|buy|explore|book|order|find out)\\b", "message": "Add one clear call to action, for example \"Shop the Vitamin C Brightening Serum\"."}
source_ref: Aurelle Brand Book v1.3 §5.1 Calls to action

title: Calls to action name the product, not "click here"
examples_good: Shop the Vitamin C Brightening Serum
source_ref: Aurelle Brand Book v1.3 §5.1 Calls to action

title: Use preferred product and ingredient names from the term list
source_ref: Aurelle Brand Book v1.3 §4 Product naming

title: Email addresses and URLs in lowercase
Don't capitalise website, internet, online or email mid-sentence
Numbers over three digits get commas
Use the % symbol, not the word percent
Em dashes without spaces
Single space between sentences
Use emoji sparingly: infrequently and deliberately
Use ellipses sparingly; not for drama
Use exclamation points sparingly (testable version: TN-02)
Be genuine: familiar, warm and accessible
